subject: QuantaHealth: SIG selection, SOC 2 status, and proposed evidence matrix
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@quantahhealth.com>, QuantaHealth Security <security@quantahhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuantaHealth: SIG selection, SOC 2 status, and proposed evidence matrix

Thanks for taking the time this morning, Emma — good to meet the team. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our discovery call so procurement/security can route this efficiently.

High-level posture (so you have context):
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering our control environment and serving runtime; a redacted report can be shared under NDA.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We operate with global data residency options and support HIPAA via a standard BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Hosting options: Hosted API (standard), Dedicated pools (tenant isolation), Private (VPC/on-prem) — each has slightly different evidence profiles.

Suggested path for QuantaHealth (based on today):
1) Start with a SIG-Lite (we find it speeds procurement for healthcare buyers) to establish scope quickly.
2) If procurement needs, we can complete full CAIQ or a custom questionnaire afterward.
3) We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II, network diagram, and an evidence matrix mapping SIG questions to artifacts.

Clarifying questions for you (so we scope the SIG-Lite correctly):
- Will QuantaHealth be sending PHI to Redwood or running models on PHI inside your environment? (important for BAA scope)
- Preferred evidence delivery method: SharePoint/Drive link vs. uploading completed SIG to your portal vs. DocuSign routing?
- Timeline: do you need the SIG completed before Oct 21 to align with your vendor committee?

Attachments: I’m attaching a one-pager and a proposed evidence matrix to show what we typically provide and where we ask for clarification. Attachments: redwood-security-one-pager.pdf (overview), proposed-evidence-matrix.csv (mapping).

Next steps (proposed):
- You confirm SIG scope (Lite vs full) and whether PHI/BAA is required.
- If SIG-Lite acceptable, we’ll return a completed SIG-Lite + redacted SOC 2 + network diagram within 5 business days (subject to NDA).
- Schedule a 30-min evidence-handoff with our security engineer if you want to walk through any items.

Thanks — I’ll pause procurement outreach until we confirm scope.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Lauren — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifying items from our side before we lock scope: 

1) SIG-Lite vs full SIG: Procurement prefers SIG-Lite where it covers the high-risk items; legal sometimes insists on full CAIQ for critical suppliers. Can you outline what you would include in the SIG-Lite deliverable vs the full SIG/CAIQ?

2) BAA: We need to confirm BAA availability up-front. Can you send a sample/draft BAA and confirm if Redwood will sign a BAA for hosted API (we may route PHI to the hosted API temporarily during pilot)?

3) Top evidence asks: to help our team triage, can you list the top 5 artifacts you’d expect to supply first (SOC2 redacted, network diagram, IAM policy, vuln scan summary, key management evidence, etc.)?

4) Timeline: we’re targeting a vendor decision window of mid-Oct (committee meets Oct 18). We’d need completed SIG-Lite + redacted SOC2 by Oct 10 to make that meeting. Is that feasible?

Also, procurement prefers delivery via our secure SharePoint tenant rather than external Drive links. If we provide a folder to drop artifacts, will that work?

Emma — thanks for the concrete asks. Quick answers below and an attached short evidence plan (I’ve also uploaded these to the shared Drive link — will copy into your SharePoint once you provide the folder).

1) SIG-Lite vs full CAIQ:
- SIG-Lite: targeted subset we prepare for quick procurement — includes governance, encryption, access control, incident response summaries and a mapped evidence matrix. Typically ~40-60 questions depending on scope.
- Full CAIQ/FAIR: full questionnaire for deep security assessments; we can fill it but it takes longer and will require more artifact collation.

2) BAA: we do provide a BAA.
- Sample attached: sample-BAA-draft.pdf
- Note: for hosted API, we can cover PHI under BAA controls but strongly recommend Dedicated/Private for long-term PHI workloads.

3) Top evidence items we’ll provide first (in order):
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II report (controls + auditor statement)
- Network diagram (redwood-network-diagram.pdf)
- IAM & least-privilege policy + role inventory
- Recent vulnerability scan summary and patch cadence note
- KMS/Key management description and certificate of rotation

4) Timeline: Oct 10 deadline — feasible if we get scope by EOD Sep 30 and an NDA for the SOC 2 redaction. Committing to SIG-Lite + redacted SOC2 + network diagram by Oct 8 if SharePoint folder is provided by Sep 30 EOD.

Delivery preferences: SharePoint is fine — please send a folder link and write permissions for upload. If you prefer, we can also upload to our secure artifact portal (link below) and share short-lived access.

Link to evidence portal (internal): https://secure.redwoodinference.com/evidence/QH-2027-0017 (we will also copy into your SharePoint on receipt).
